title: The Doctor Who Harvested 1,000 Eyes from Living Patients
hook: In 1930s India, a British surgeon removed the eyes of poor patients without consent—and sold them to wealthy buyers.
why_this_can_go_viral: The visceral horror of living victims being blinded triggers immediate emotional reaction and share impulse.

title: The Secret Map That Shows a Hidden 7th Continent
hook: A 16th-century Vatican map reveals a landmass in the South Pacific—one that doesn't exist on any modern globe.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that an entire continent was erased sparks conspiracy curiosity and map-tracing engagement.

title: The Empire That Made Prisoners Fight Crocodiles for Sport
hook: In 19th-century Madagascar, Queen Ranavalona I fed political prisoners to crocodiles in front of cheering crowds.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme royal cruelty mixed with animal brutality creates shock value that drives shares.

title: The Colony Where Children Were Raised by Wolves
hook: A 17th-century English colony abandoned 12 orphaned children in the wilderness—and they survived by joining a wolf pack.
why_this_can_go_viral: The primal survival story of children raised by animals taps into deep evolutionary curiosity.

title: The Buried City That Had Running Water Before Rome
hook: Deep in the Amazon, archaeologists found a lost city with aqueducts and plumbing—built 1,500 years before the Romans.
why_this_can_go_viral: Rewriting history with superior ancient tech creates 'we were lied to' engagement.

title: The King Who Collected 10,000 Human Skulls as Decor
hook: King Rwabugiri of Rwanda turned his palace into a shrine of skulls—one from every enemy he personally killed.
why_this_can_go_viral: The sheer scale of personal violence combined with macabre decor is horrifyingly shareable.

title: The Secret Vatican Archives That Prove Popes Knew About Atlantis
hook: A locked room in the Vatican contains maps and documents describing a lost Atlantic continent—with human remains that don't match any known species.
why_this_can_go_viral: Atlantis + Vatican secrecy is a proven viral combination that fuels endless speculation.

title: The Empire That Sacrificed 80,000 People in One Day
hook: At the 1487 dedication of the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan, Aztec priests killed 80,000 prisoners in a single sunrise-to-sunset ritual.
why_this_can_go_viral: The scale of 80,000 deaths in one day is almost incomprehensible, forcing viewers to engage.

title: The Town Where a Volcano Erupted—and Everyone Stayed Because They Were Told It Was Safe
hook: In 1985, Colombian officials assured Armero residents the volcano was harmless—hours before 25,000 died in a mudslide.
why_this_can_go_viral: Authority betrayal leading to mass death is a universally angering story that demands sharing.
